diagnostics_before_registration: Not gate data. cr15a_diag5 (before vs v3 code, preload, 6 reps): right after the many-files batch the glibc heap in use is c1 28.5 vs 33.0 MiB; after gc.collect + 3 s both sides RssAnon ~39-40 MiB, after malloc_trim 37.4-37.6 MiB, heap in use 10.25 vs 10.26 MiB. cr15a_diag6 (4 reps): 3 s without GC releases nothing; a DEBUG_SAVEALL pass finds the downloaded bodies in cyclic garbage on BOTH sides (c1 before 9-15 bodies / after 16-18, c8 35-42 / 38-42). Local cycle probe (MockTransport): every download leaves Response <-> BoundAsyncStream (httpx) in a cycle with its body, before and after alike; the extra counting wrapper only shifts the GC timing. With the v5 stream swap the probe finds 0 bodies in cyclic garbage.
change: v4 code (IndexerClient.get_bounded: streamed GET under the adapter semaphore, declared-length precheck, decoded-byte cap indexer_torrent_max_bytes = 48 MiB (user decision 2026-11-07), session-error relogin retry and redirect history kept; download_torrent uses it; identity bodies run httpx aread() over a counting raw-stream wrapper and return the original response; encoded bodies count decoded bytes) plus: after aread() the identity path replaces response.stream with httpx.ByteStream(response.content), breaking the Response <-> stream reference cycle so the body is freed by reference counting. Regression test: the response is released with the GC disabled.
